title: Normalize session token tallies for partial and aborted websocket flows
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
We are seeing discrepancies between provisional token tallies reported during WebSocket streaming sessions and the final billed token counts for sessions that were interrupted, resumed, or switched models mid-stream. This causes both under- and over-charging in edge cases and confuses quota enforcement.

Scope & Symptoms:
- Occurs mainly for long-running interactive sessions (>60s) with intermittent client reconnects and midstream model handoffs.
- Root cause hypothesis: fragmented client frames are being credited immediately by the ingestion layer (provisional credits) but the final aggregation step in the metering pipeline either (a) drops orphan fragments after an abort or (b) double-counts fragments when resume/fan-in occurs.
- Impact: ~0.2% of streaming sessions show >5% divergence between provisional and final counts; affects quota checks and billing exports (invoice mismatch reports).

Investigation log (high-level):
- 2025-08-11: Triage meeting. Scoped to websocket/streaming path and quota enforcement. Assigned to Diego.
- 2025-08-12: Reproduced in staging with synthetic client that simulates reconnect and midstream model switch. Captured traces and fragment IDs.
- 2025-08-15: Added verbose logs to ingress + aggregator. Identified missing deterministic fragment IDs on client resume (ingress generated new fragment IDs, causing aggregator to treat resumed content as new session).
- 2025-08-20: Prototyped change to persist session-level fragment watermark and deterministic resume token.
- 2025-08-25: Wrote unit tests for aggregator idempotency. Verified local aggregator dedupe works but end-to-end still shows race between accounting writer and finalization job.

Proposed design changes:
1) Deterministic fragment IDs: ingress will accept client-sent resume_token when present; otherwise generate a stable {session_id}.{seq} id. This allows aggregator to dedupe across reconnects.
2) Soft-commit semantics: provisioning credits emitted by ingress become provisional and are tagged with provisional_id. Final commit happens when aggregator emits FINALIZED event. Billing writer treats provisional credits as non-final until commit or TTL expiry.
3) Finalizer job: a periodic reconciliation job will scan in-flight sessions >30s without finalization and reconcile by replaying ordered fragments into the aggregator to produce deterministic final counts.
4) Backfill tool: allow backfilling historical ambiguous sessions using preserved frame traces.

Trade-offs and rationale:
- Delaying final commit (soft-commit) adds a small window where quotas may be slightly conservative; this prevents overcharging but may reject some requests that rely on immediate credit availability. We limit this by using short provisional TTL (default 60s) and by preferring fast-path commits for clients that signal explicit end-of-stream.
- Metadata storage: maintaining provisional state increases memory and storage overhead at the aggregator; mitigated by TTL compaction and sampling for very long sessions.

Testing & rollout plan:
- Unit tests for deterministic id generation and aggregator dedupe (done).
- Integration tests: simulated reconnect, midstream model switch, and injected out-of-order frames (in progress).
- Load test in staging: target 1000 concurrent streaming sessions with induced reconnects; measure divergence before/after. Preliminary staging run shows divergence reduced from 0.25% to 0.01% on peak.
- Canary rollout: feature-flagged update to ingress + aggregator + billing writer; initial 2% traffic for 48h, observe Grafana metering mismatch/overcharge panels.
- Full rollout: enable 100% after 7 days of canary stability.

Telemetry & dashboards:
- New Grafana panel tracks provisional_vs_final_delta (per minute) and sessions_reconciled_by_finalizer.
- Alerts: trigger P1 if provisional_vs_final_delta >1% for 5m on production. Dashboard link: https://grafana.redwood.net/d/abc123/metering-errors

Artifacts & links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.net/display/BILL/Deterministic+Fragment+IDs+and+Soft-Commit
- PR with ingress + aggregator changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/12345
- Backfill script: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/blob/main/tools/metering_backfill.py
- Staging load test results: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1a2b3c-metering-load-test

Open questions & follow-ups:
- Should provisionals count toward hard quota usage until finalization? (Current proposal: provisional usage is visible in console as tentative usage but does not decrement hard quota until final commit.)
- What max TTL is acceptable for customers with regulatory requirements? (Add label to customer profile to bypass soft-commit TTL.)
- Long term: explore moving to event-sourced ledger for metering to guarantee strong consistency at cost of write amplification.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end tests show <0.05% sessions with >2% token-count divergence under the staged test profile.
- No spike in legitimate request rejections attributable to provisional semantics during 2% canary.
- Billing export matches reconciled final counts for canary traffic window.

Checklist:
- [x] Triage & reproduce
- [x] Unit tests for aggregator dedupe
- [x] Ingress deterministic ID change PR opened
- [ ] Integration tests for end-to-end accounting
- [ ] Finalizer job implemented and smoke-tested
- [ ] Canary rollout & observe
- [ ] Full rollout
